objects.description: Opaque setup object that holds precomputed, read-only data (e.g., twiddle factors) for performing PFFFT transforms. It is shared-safe across threads because it contains only read-only state. The actual struct layout is intentionally hidden in the implementation.
Enumeration specifying the transform direction: forward FFT or backward (inverse) FFT. Used by transform and reorder functions.
Enumeration specifying the transform type configured for a setup: real-valued or complex-valued transforms.

functions.name: pffft_new_setup
functions.description: Allocate and initialize an opaque PFFFT_Setup that holds precomputed twiddle factors and parameters for transforms of size N and the given transform type (PFFFT_REAL or PFFFT_COMPLEX). The setup is read-only and can be shared across threads. Returns NULL if N is not supported (e.g., not decomposable as required or too large).
requirements: Callers must check for a NULL return to handle unsupported sizes.
The returned PFFFT_Setup is read-only and may be shared by many threads.
The setup must be destroyed with pffft_destroy_setup when no longer needed.

functions.name: pffft_destroy_setup
functions.description: Destroy and free a PFFFT_Setup previously created by pffft_new_setup. Safe to call when you are done with all transforms using that setup.
requirements: The argument must be a PFFFT_Setup pointer previously returned by pffft_new_setup (i.e., not an arbitrary pointer).
The setup must not be used after being destroyed.

functions.name: pffft_transform
functions.signature: void pffft_transform(PFFFT_Setup *setup, const float *input, float *output, float *work, pffft_direction_t direction);
functions.description: Perform a forward or backward Fourier transform using the given setup. The output is stored in an internal (implementation-efficient) order suitable for inverse transforms and convolution; use pffft_transform_ordered or pffft_zreorder to obtain interleaved complex order. Transforms are unscaled: backward(forward(x)) = N*x; callers typically scale the backward result by 1/N. The temporary work area should point to N floats (real) or 2*N floats (complex); if work is NULL, a stack buffer is used. input and output may alias.
requirements: setup must be a valid PFFFT_Setup created for the intended transform type (PFFFT_REAL or PFFFT_COMPLEX) and the data length N.
All float* buffers (input, output, work when non-NULL) must be SIMD-aligned (16-byte alignment on x86 and PowerPC), as stated for all float pointers in this API.
If work is provided, it must reference space for N floats for real transforms or 2*N floats for complex transforms.
input and output may alias; this is explicitly allowed.
Direction must be either PFFFT_FORWARD or PFFFT_BACKWARD.
Callers should scale the PFFFT_BACKWARD result by 1/N if a unitary transform is desired.

functions.name: pffft_transform_ordered
functions.signature: void pffft_transform_ordered(PFFFT_Setup *setup, const float *input, float *output, float *work, pffft_direction_t direction);
functions.description: Perform a forward or backward transform like pffft_transform, but ensure that the output is in the canonical interleaved complex order. Equivalent to calling pffft_transform followed by pffft_zreorder. input and output may alias.
requirements: setup must be a valid PFFFT_Setup created by pffft_new_setup for the data length and transform type.
All float* buffers (input, output, work when non-NULL) must be SIMD-aligned (16-byte alignment on x86 and PowerPC).
If work is provided, it must reference space for N floats for real transforms or 2*N floats for complex transforms.
input and output may alias; this is explicitly allowed.
Direction must be PFFFT_FORWARD or PFFFT_BACKWARD.
Backward transform results are unscaled; callers typically scale by 1/N if required.

functions.name: pffft_zreorder
functions.signature: void pffft_zreorder(PFFFT_Setup *setup, const float *input, float *output, pffft_direction_t direction);
functions.description: Reorder frequency-domain data between PFFFT’s internal ordering and canonical interleaved complex order. Call with direction=PFFFT_FORWARD after a forward pffft_transform to obtain standard order, and with direction=PFFFT_BACKWARD before a backward transform if data is in canonical order. For real transforms, DC and Nyquist terms are packed as F(0)+i*F(N/2+1) in the first entry. input and output should not alias.
requirements: setup must be a valid PFFFT_Setup for the transform size/type of the data being reordered.
input and output must not alias (they must be distinct buffers).
All float* buffers must be SIMD-aligned (16-byte alignment on x86 and PowerPC).
direction must be PFFFT_FORWARD when converting internal-order forward-FFT output to canonical order; use PFFFT_BACKWARD for the reverse operation.

functions.name: pffft_zconvolve_accumulate
functions.signature: void pffft_zconvolve_accumulate(PFFFT_Setup *setup, const float *dft_a, const float *dft_b, float *dft_ab, float scaling);
functions.description: Multiply frequency components of two spectra and accumulate into a destination buffer in PFFFT’s internal frequency layout. Intended for convolution in the frequency domain. The inputs must be forward-transform outputs from pffft_transform and must not have been reordered by pffft_zreorder. Performs: dft_ab += (dft_a * dft_b) * scaling. The three pointers may alias.
requirements: setup must be a valid PFFFT_Setup matching the transform size/type of the spectra.
dft_a and dft_b must be outputs of pffft_transform with direction=PFFFT_FORWARD and must not have been reordered by pffft_zreorder.
dft_ab must be in the same internal layout as produced by pffft_transform (i.e., not reordered).
dft_a, dft_b, and dft_ab may alias; this is explicitly allowed.
All float* buffers must be SIMD-aligned (16-byte alignment on x86 and PowerPC).
scaling is an arbitrary float multiplier; no specific constraints are documented.

functions.name: pffft_aligned_malloc
functions.description: Allocate a memory block of nb_bytes with the proper SIMD-compatible alignment required by PFFFT (16-byte alignment on x86 and PowerPC). Use this to obtain correctly aligned float buffers for the transform APIs.
requirements: nb_bytes specifies the number of bytes to allocate; must be large enough for the intended buffers.
The returned pointer must be freed with pffft_aligned_free.
Alignment is intended to satisfy the "simd-compatible" requirement (16-byte on x86/PowerPC).

functions.name: pffft_aligned_free
requirements: The pointer must have been returned by pffft_aligned_malloc (or be NULL).
Do not use the memory after it has been freed.

functions.name: pffft_simd_size
functions.description: Return 4 or 1 depending on whether support for SSE/Altivec instructions was enabled when building pffft.c. Useful to query SIMD width capability at runtime.
requirements: No arguments; callable at any time.
Interpret return value: 4 indicates SIMD support enabled; 1 indicates scalar fallback.

data_types.description: Arbitrary bytes interpreted as a contiguous array of IEEE-754 single-precision floats. The buffer length is determined by the caller (N floats for real transforms, 2*N floats for complex transforms). Any byte sequence is accepted; unspecified bytes beyond provided data may be zero-padded.
